headline: Highest risk is medium: Prefect can egress broadly while Superset can egress via allowlisted APIs, creating default-path data movement and workflow-to-dashboard trust issues; no direct prompt-injection or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel or parser is documented, so direct injection is not evidenced. However, Prefect can move workflow metadata over broad egress and Superset can call its API, so a manual copy/paste or file bridge could carry malicious content. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies Prefect output into Superset text fields or dashboards
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is introduced between the two
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste policy with no raw HTML/markdown transfer
Add content sanitization before importing Prefect outputs into Superset
Restrict shared folders to read-only for one side
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Prefect touches workflow metadata and has broad egress, while Superset touches no declared sensitive data and only has allowlisted API egress. The pair can leak metadata if operators place sensitive files in a shared workspace, but the profile does not show default shared storage or secret handling, so blast radius appears limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace containing sensitive workflow metadata
IF Prefect outputs are forwarded into Superset without redaction
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared workspace
Redact workflow metadata before publishing to Superset
Disable unnecessary exports from Prefect runs
requires-engineering: separate storage buckets per agent

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents are data-engineering tools with network egress, but neither profile shows filesystem write, git mutation, or overlapping OAuth scopes. The main conflict is operational contention over shared APIs or datasets, which is possible but not documented as default and is unlikely to cause severe corruption.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same external API or dataset
IF an orchestrator routes both through the same mutable resource without locking
mitigations: Limit each agent to distinct datasets
Add a simple lock or queue around shared writes
requires-engineering: enforce optimistic concurrency on shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect can generate workflow metadata that Superset may ingest or display, and Superset exposes an API surface that could act on that input. There is no verification step documented between them, so erroneous Prefect output could cascade into misleading dashboards or downstream actions in default integrations.
conditions: IF Superset ingests Prefect-produced metadata without validation
IF downstream users treat Superset visualizations as authoritative
mitigations: Add schema validation before Superset ingestion
Mark Prefect-derived fields as untrusted in dashboards
Require human review for any action triggered from Superset
requires-engineering: insert a verification service between the agents

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data class mismatch is documented. Prefect only lists workflow metadata, and Superset lists no data classes touched, so there is no evidenced compliance pathway requiring a higher severity. The other agent is not cited separately because no cross-border or regulated-data flow is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into either agent
IF a future deployment adds conflicting retention or residency settings
mitigations: Document retention settings for both tools
Keep regulated data out of this pair unless controls are added
